messages.content: Plan a relaxed 2-day trip to Yosemite for a first-time visitor who prefers easy walks and scenic viewpoints. Do not check live conditions.

Solo trip, two easy days, valley-focused — Yosemite's classic viewpoints are almost all walkable without breaking a sweat. Here's how I'd lay it out.

## At a glance
- Fly into Fresno (FAT, ~1.5hr to the valley) or drive in from the Bay Area (~3.5-4hr) — Yosemite Valley is the hub for everything below.
- Entrance fee is typically $35 per vehicle, good for 7 days.
- August in the valley usually runs warm and dry, mid-70s to mid-90s by afternoon — mornings are the move for comfort and lighter crowds.
- Base yourself in Yosemite Valley (Yosemite Valley Lodge or Curry Village) so you're not driving much — the free shuttle loop covers most of what's below.
- Parking at the main day-use lots typically fills by mid-morning in summer — arrive before 9am or plan to shuttle from Curry Village.
- Everything on this plan is flat or gently graded — no scrambles, no exposure, nothing over 2 miles.
- Worth a quick look at current alerts for Yosemite on TrailVerse before you go, since Glacier Point Road access and any valley closures can shift.

## Day 1 — Valley Icons
**Morning:** Start at Tunnel View for the classic postcard shot of El Capitan, Half Dome, and Bridalveil Fall — 5 minutes from the car, no walking required. From there, head to Bridalveil Fall Trail, a short paved 0.5-mile round trip to the base of the falls (mist is refreshing in summer heat).

**Midday:** Grab lunch at Yosemite Valley Lodge or the Village Store, then walk the Lower Yosemite Fall Trail — a flat 1-mile loop right to the base of North America's tallest waterfall. Fully paved, stroller/wheelchair friendly.

**Afternoon:** Wander the Cook's Meadow Loop (1 mile, flat), which gives you open views of Half Dome, Sentinel Rock, and Yosemite Falls all from one easy trail. Great light in late afternoon.

**Evening:** Dinner at the Mountain Room Restaurant or Degnan's Kitchen in the valley, then catch sunset from Sentinel Bridge — one of the best reflection shots of Half Dome in the Merced River.

## Day 2 — Mirror Lake & Glacier Point
**Morning:** Mirror Lake Trail — a flat, easy 2-mile round trip along the Merced River to the lake, usually quiet before 9am. Good wildlife-watching stretch.

**Midday:** Drive up to Glacier Point (about 1 hour from the valley, road typically open summer through fall). It's a short paved walk from the parking area to one of the best panoramic overlooks in the park — Half Dome at eye level, valley floor 3,200 feet below.

**Afternoon:** Head back down and, if you've got energy, swing by Mariposa Grove for the Big Trees Loop — a 0.3-mile wheelchair-accessible walk among giant sequoias. Note: this adds about an hour of driving each way, so it's the first thing to cut if you'd rather linger in the valley instead.

**Evening:** Wind down back in the valley — sunset at Valley View along Southside Drive is an easy pull-off with a gorgeous reflection shot, no walking needed.

## Don't Forget
- Refillable water bottle — filling stations are at the visitor center and lodges
- Sun protection — the valley floor has little shade midday
- Layers for morning cool-down, especially near the falls
- Bear-proof food storage if you're picnicking outdoors (lockers provided at trailheads)
- Cash or card for the shuttle-adjacent food stands — cell coverage is spotty throughout the valley

## Estimated Costs (solo, 2 days)
- Entrance: $35 (vehicle, 7-day pass)
- Lodging: ~$250-300/night at Yosemite Valley Lodge, or ~$150-200 at Curry Village
- Food: ~$50-60/day
- Total: roughly $450-650 depending on lodging choice
Can you make Day 2 even more relaxed and keep the total walking for that day under 2 miles?

Easy fix — swapping out Mirror Lake and Mariposa Grove since together those push well past 2 miles once you add the driving and standing-around at each stop.

Here's the revised Day 2:

**Morning (relaxed start):** Skip the early alarm — grab coffee at the lodge, then take a short stroll at Swinging Bridge picnic area, a flat 0.5-mile loop along the Merced River. Quiet, shaded, good Half Dome views without any real walking.

**Midday:** Drive up to Glacier Point (about 1 hour, mostly scenic pullouts along the way). The overlook itself is a paved 0.3-mile round trip from the parking lot — bench seating right at the rim if you just want to sit and take in Half Dome and the valley floor 3,200 feet below. Pack a picnic lunch and eat up there instead of rushing back down.

**Afternoon:** Casual drive back into the valley with a stop at Valley View along Southside Drive — a pull-off right at the river's edge, zero walking required, and one of the best reflection shots in the park.

**Evening:** Back at the lodge with time to spare. If you want a last little wander, a quiet 0.3-mile stretch near Sentinel Bridge at dusk rounds things out — otherwise just relax and let Day 1 be the more active day.

Total walking: about 1.1 miles, all flat and paved. This trades the Mirror Lake hike and the Mariposa Grove side trip for more time sitting at viewpoints instead of covering ground — a better fit for the pace you're after. If you'd rather skip the Glacier Point drive too and stay entirely in the valley, I can swap that in for something like a longer lunch at the Ahwahnee and an easy loop near the meadow instead.
